title: Suspected mpox admissions to a dedicated infectious-diseases isolation ward in northeastern Nigeria, 2022–2025: a register-based descriptive study with evidence of a household cluster

analysis.research_question_and_background: Mpox has re-emerged as a public-health priority across Nigeria, and successive international public-health emergencies were declared in 2022 and 2024. analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a register-based descriptive study of all admissions to the infectious-diseases isolation ward of Modibbo Adama University Teaching Hospital, Yola, in which mpox was recorded as the working or a differential diagnosis between February 2022 and January 2025.
analysis.methods: Age, sex, month of admission, locality, recorded clinical impression, and outcome were abstracted and summarised, with proportions reported using Wilson 95% confidence intervals.

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Cases were clinically suspected rather than laboratory-confirmed, which is the principal limitation of this study.

The study highlights the need for improved laboratory diagnosis and reporting. However, the reliance on clinical suspicion rather than laboratory confirmation is a key limitation.

title: Evaluating search-enabled large language model interfaces for mpox public health consultation: a guideline-based comparative study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Background Search-enabled large language model interfaces are increasingly used by the public for health information, but their performance in mpox-related public health consultation remains unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study evaluated their safety, accuracy, empathy, reliability/information quality, and readability. We conducted a single-query comparative cross-sectional evaluation using 52 predefined mpox-related public consultation questions. Each question was submitted once to each of six search-enabled LLM interfaces, yielding 312 first responses.
analysis.methods: Responses were assessed against a guideline-based reference framework. Safety was coded as a binary outcome, while accuracy and empathy were rated on 5-point scales. Reliability/information quality was evaluated using DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA benchmark criteria, and GQS. Readability was assessed using six established readability indices. Five trained raters independently evaluated the human-scored outcomes.
analysis.main_results: Unsafe responses were relatively infrequent but occurred in all six interfaces, with safe-response rates ranging from 86.5 to 92.3%. No pairwise difference in Safety remained statistically significant after Benjamini–Hochberg correction. Overall differences across interfaces were statistically significant for Accuracy, Empathy, all four reliability/information quality measures, and all six readability indices.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted post hoc analyses identified outcome-specific pairwise differences, although the pairwise patterns varied across measures. The evaluated search-enabled LLM interfaces showed heterogeneous performance across safety, accuracy, empathy, reliability/information quality, and readability.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the need for guideline-based evaluation, source transparency, readability optimization, and robust safety safeguards when such interfaces are evaluated or considered for mpox-related public health consultation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The results represent a time- and configuration-specific interface-level snapshot; they should not be attributed to the underlying base models in isolation or interpreted as establishing reproducible performance or a stable hierarchy across sessions, versions, or settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the performance of six search-enabled large language model (LLM) interfaces in mpox-related public health consultation. The research aimed to assess safety, accuracy, empathy, reliability/information quality, and readability of responses to 52 predefined mpox-related questions. Each question was submitted to all six interfaces, resulting in 312 responses. The responses were evaluated using a guideline-based reference framework, with safety as a binary outcome, accuracy and empathy on 5-point scales, reliability/information quality using DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA benchmark criteria, and GQS, and readability using six established indices. The results showed that unsafe responses were relatively infrequent but occurred in all interfaces, with safe-response rates ranging from 86.5 to 92.3%. However, overall differences across interfaces were statistically significant for accuracy, empathy, reliability/information quality, and readability. The study highlights the need for guideline-based evaluation, source transparency, readability optimization, and safety safeguards for LLM interfaces used in mpox-related public health consultation. title: Stability and sensitivity analysis of transmission dynamics of Mpox virus

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to analyze the transmission dynamics of Mpox virus through stability and sensitivity analysis to understand the factors influencing its spread and inform control strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A deterministic compartmental model was formulated to study Mpox transmission dynamics in interacting human and rodent populations, with the human population divided into susceptible, exposed, infectious, quarantined, and recovered classes, and the rodent population into susceptible, exposed, and infectious classes.
analysis.methods: The study used a deterministic compartmental model, incorporating a quarantined-to-susceptible pathway to account for undetected cases. The basic reproduction number $R_0$ was calculated using the next-generation matrix method, and stability of equilibria was analyzed using Routh-Hurwitz conditions and Castillo-Chavez and Song approaches.
analysis.main_results: The basic reproduction number $R_0$ was derived, and it was found that the human-to-human transmission rate and the proportion of exposed humans entering the infectious class are the dominant drivers of transmission. Increasing recovery and treatment rates was shown to reduce $R_0$.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings provide a quantitative understanding of the key factors driving Mpox transmission and highlight the importance of contact reduction and improved treatment coverage in controlling the disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results offer a foundation for designing targeted interventions to reduce Mpox transmission, particularly by focusing on contact tracing and enhancing treatment protocols.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a deterministic model, which may not fully capture real-world complexities such as stochasticity or variability in transmission rates. The evidence is strong for the model's stability analysis but limited in its applicability to real-world scenarios without further empirical validation.

The model incorporates a quarantined-to-susceptible pathway to account for undetected cases. The results indicate that human-to-human transmission rate and proportion of exposed humans entering the infectious class are the main drivers of Mpox spread. analysis.methods: The proposed architecture integrates a Highly Efficient Channel Attention (HECA) mechanism into YOLOv11, applying Global Average Pooling and Max Average Pooling to input feature maps, and augments a dataset containing monkeypox, measles, chickenpox, and normal skin images using spatial transformations and pixel-domain enhancements.
analysis.main_results: On the test set, HECA-YOLOv11 achieved 98.9% accuracy, 99% precision, 99.3% recall, and 99.1% F1-score, outperforming EfficientNet-v2-l, GoogLeNet, ResNet50, VGG19, MobileNetv2, DenseNet201, YOLOv11s, SE-YOLOv11, and ECA-YOLOv11 by over 5.1% across all metrics.

title: Monkeypox Virus Surveillance in Wastewater, North Carolina, USA, October 2023–May 2025

analysis.research_question_and_background: Since the first mpox case in a nonendemic region, mpox has become an increasing public health concern in the United States, prompting the need for improved surveillance methods beyond clinical case reporting.
analysis.study_design_and_population: During October 29, 2023–May 2025, 801 wastewater samples were collected from 16 treatment plants serving approximately 2 million residents in North Carolina, USA.
analysis.methods: Wastewater samples were analyzed using the CDC Non-variola Orthopoxvirus Generic Real-Time PCR Test, with viral gene copies normalized to flow rate and population within the sewershed. The assay limit of detection was theoretically estimated at 500 copies/L, and a +17-day alignment window was used to assess temporal concordance with reported clinical cases.
analysis.main_results: The overall sensitivity of wastewater detection for identifying temporally aligned reported mpox cases was 10.6% (95% CI 6.5%–16.7%), increasing to 1.4% (95% CI 0.4%–5.0%) when restricted to detections above the limit of detection. Specificity was high (95.1% to 97.7%), and negative predictive value was approximately 83%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that wastewater surveillance provides complementary public health awareness despite low sensitivity, as wastewater detections without temporally aligned cases may reflect unrecognized infections rather than false positives.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Wastewater surveillance can complement clinical case reporting for mpox by providing high specificity and negative predictive value, particularly in low-incidence settings, though sensitivity remains limited for early warning.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s reliance on reported clinical cases as an imperfect reference standard limits diagnostic accuracy estimation, and restricting to detections above the limit of detection markedly reduces sensitivity, potentially compromising early warning capacity.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated monkeypox virus (MPXV) surveillance in wastewater across 16 treatment plants in North Carolina, USA, from October 2023 to May 2025, analyzing 801 samples. Using the CDC Non-variola Orthopoxvirus Generic Real-Time PCR Test, viral gene copies were quantified and normalized to flow rate and population. The assay’s theoretical limit of detection was 500 copies/L, and a +17-day alignment window assessed temporal concordance with 45 reported clinical cases. Wastewater detection showed low sensitivity (10.6% overall; 1.4% above LOD) but high specificity (>95%) and moderate negative predictive value (~83%). Sensitivity increased when trace detections were included, suggesting low-level signals contribute to temporal alignment. The authors conclude that wastewater surveillance complements clinical reporting by providing high specificity and negative predictive value, though sensitivity remains limited for early warning.
